string-array.name: help_items
string-array.item: Basic browsing operations:\n By default, swiping up navigates to the previous item. Swiping down navigates to the next item.\n However you can change this behavior in the action settings.
Main Menu: \n By default, use the down right swipe to open the menu, swipe right to expand more options.\n You can display all menu items at once by customizing it in the settings.

voice assistant:
 By default, the voice assistant is activated with the down left swipe gesture and the command is spoken after the sound. Tapping the screen will force the immediate recognition
 The voice assistant can be customized in advanced settings, voice assistant settings, voice assistant capabilities settings.
Actions menu: \n By default, up right swipe opens the action menu, right swipe expands the menu and double tap activates the focused menu option.

Extensions:
 By default, the first and last left gestures are used to open the extension list, and then right-slide to open the voice command list, and double-click to execute the corresponding function.
 You can find more plugins in the resource download.
 Advanced settings, voice assistant settings, voice command settings, new, modified or downloaded

Copy, append copy, clipboard and favorites:
 These functions can be found in the operation menu.
 Copy, copy the focus to the clipboard
 Append copy to append the focus content to the last item of the clipboard,
 Clipboard, record the most recently copied content, click to enter the edit box, long press to add content to favorites
 Favorites, click to enter the edit box, long press to edit,
 In advanced settings, resource management can delete or backup clipboard and favorites

Long copy (premium users only):
 Long copy can copy long list content.
 After the long copy is activated in the operation menu, you need to wait for different time according to the length of the list. When the copy is completed, you will be prompted to complete the long copy.
 During long copying, you can force abort by swiping any gesture.

Full text selection (Premium users only):\n Full-text selection is mainly suitable for copying some content from web pages or longer content. The full text selection can split the content by word, sentence, and segment form, select the required content through the check box form, and finally copy,\n In the content list, you can long press an item as the starting point, and then long press the end of the selection to quickly select multiple consecutive items.

Advanced editing (member function):
 You can edit the focus content according to words, sentences, paragraphs or full text in the edit box or non-edit box to facilitate quick positioning and modification.
 Click on the split edit list to edit it, long press to make the entry more detailed split.
 Edit box can be clicked to enter the edit box, and the non-edit box can only be saved to the clipboard by copying.
List browsing:\n Display all the focus as a list, click to activate the corresponding focus, especially suitable for use on web pages.
Reading mode (member function):\n You can read webpage articles opened by the browser, filter unwanted content, and turn pages automatically.

Virtual screen (member function):\n The OCR recognizes the content on the screen, displays the result according to the text position, clicks the result text to activate the corresponding focus, long presses the word to split the focus, and clicks the word to activate the position of the corresponding word.\n Android 7 or above double-click to activate, Android 6 below three times to activate.

Text recognition (member function):\n The content on the screen is recognized by the OCR, and the result is displayed in a list form, and the result list is clicked to activate the corresponding focus, the long press is followed by the word display result, and the single word is activated to activate the position of the corresponding word.\n Clicking is not supported under Android 6 and only results can be viewed.

Captcha identification (member function):\n Touch the verification code focus, use advanced menu, verification code identification, or voice assistant, verification code identification, can recognize English or digital verification code, and the recognition result is automatically copied to the clipboard.

Jieshuo camera (member function):\n The camera can recognize text, scenes, animals, plants, or for camera guidance. The camera currently supports only the rear camera, using volume plus shooting, volume minus switching mode.

Quickly navigate between list items:\n In the operation settings, left and right shortcut gesture settings enable the left and right gestures to move quickly in the list, you can use the left or right gesture to quickly browse the message in the list of QQ messages, for example.

Notification black/whitelist:
 The notification blacklist can filter out notifications containing the specified content, and input an asterisk to filter all notifications of the application.
 The notification whitelist can allow reading of notifications containing the specified content, even if the notification has been closed, entering an asterisk indicates that all notifications for the program are allowed.
 Keywords support regular expressions.

Content blacklist:\n You can filter the focus content of the specified content, usually used to filter some non-standard accessibility instructions.\n Regular expressions are not supported based on efficiency considerations.

Web content filtering (member function):\n Filters the useless image annotations on the page to filter out the lengthy and useless instructions on the page.\n Stronger filtering can further filter out unnecessary non-essential content.

Powerful mode (member function):\n Powerful mode gives you more operational focus,\n It is known to bring better experiences in software such as WeChat Sports, WeChat Friends Circle, Taobao Footprint, Huawei Router and so on.

Virtual navigation (member function):
 Virtual navigation can add the location of content that cannot be directly clicked to the navigation list.
 Please add only the focus of the immutable position, click on the recognized focus input name in the recognition click to add,
 Only supports Android 7 or above.

Custom gestures:
 You can customize any built-in or extended features as gestures.
 Quickly change gestures by importing a gesture pack.
 After the gesture is imported, it needs to be set in the operation, and the gesture scheme switching can take effect.
 If you are not familiar with the operation suggestions in the common settings, customize the gesture to modify the gesture.

Two-step gestures (member function):
 A two-step gesture is an operation that quickly operates a second gesture after a traditional gesture operation is completed.
 It can be turned on or customized in the action settings, two-step gestures,
 After the two-step gesture is turned on, there is a half-second delay after the first gesture operation is completed, waiting for the second step.
 Don't set gestures that require efficiency, such as moving focus gestures, using two-step gestures.

Record voice commands:\n Start the voice assistant to say the recording command, say the program to be opened in turn or click the key of the focus to realize the rapid voice command production. When all the instructions are finished, say to end the recording, after the prompt to enter the name of the command, say the name of the command, and finally say determine.\n If there is an unrecognized instruction during the recording process, you can re-speak it. Recorded commands can be changed in Advanced Settings, Voice Assistant Settings, Voice Command Settings.

Automatic message reading:
Free users can automatically read new messages in chat apps.
Premium users can also read messages from supported live-streaming apps, including Douyin, Huoshan, and Now.
Configure this feature under Content settings, Content change settings, Automatic chat-message reading.

resources.string-array:
Jieshuo multifunction gestures and extensions combine Lua syntax with the Jieshuo API to perform multiple actions with one gesture. If you know Lua and AndroLua, you can create more advanced features. This guide covers only the Jieshuo-specific API.
Basic concept:
service is the accessibility service and the core of the screen reader. All features operate through this service.
Parameter types:
node: the node with accessibility focus; most actions operate on this node.
bool: a Boolean value, true or false.
text: text content.
return tells the screen reader whether to perform the gesture's default action. Return true to intercept the gesture. Return false to pass it to the next level: an app-specific gesture passes to the global gesture, and a global gesture passes to the default gesture.
Common command:
service.execute("command",node)
Runs a built-in Jieshuo command. Returns true on success and false on failure.
service.postExecute(delay,"command",node)
Runs a command after a delay.
text=service.getText(node)
Gets the text of the specified node.
service.setText(node,text)
Sets the text of the specified edit field.
service.setText(text)
Sets the text of the focused edit field on the current screen.
service.copy()
Copies the focused node's text to the clipboard.
service.appendCopy()
Appends the focused node's text to the clipboard.
service.copy(text)
Copies the specified text to the clipboard.
service.appendCopy(text)
Appends the specified text to the clipboard.
service.paste()
Pastes clipboard content into the focused edit field.
service.paste(node)
Pastes clipboard content into the specified edit field.
service.toNext()
Moves to the next focus.
service.toNext(node,bool)
Moves to the next focus from node. If bool is true, child nodes are searched; if false, they are not.
service.toPrevious()
Moves to the previous focus.
service.toPrevious(node,bool)
Moves to the previous focus from node. If bool is true, child nodes are searched; if false, they are not.
service.toNextChar()
Moves to the next character.
service.toPreviousChar()
Moves to the previous character.
service.toNextLine()
Moves to the next line.
service.toPreviousLine()
Moves to the previous line.
service.toTextStart()
Moves to the start of the text.
service.toTextEnd()
Moves to the end of the text.
service.toListViewStart()
Moves to the start of the list.
service.toListViewEnd()
Moves to the end of the list.
service.getRootNodeInfo()
Gets the root node.
service.ocr(node)
Recognizes text in the specified node. Premium feature.
service.setTimerMode(bool)
Enables timer mode when bool is true and disables it when false.
service.setAutoReadEnabled(bool)
Enables reading mode when bool is true and disables it when false.
service.setAutoNext(bool)
Enables automatic browsing when bool is true and disables it when false.
bool=service.isEditView(node)
Checks whether node is an edit field.
bool=service.isSeekBar(node)
Checks whether node is a seek bar.
bool=service.isListView(node)
Checks whether node is a list.
bool=service.isInListView(node)
Checks whether node is inside a list.
bool=service.isInWebView(node)
Checks whether node is inside a web view.
bool=service.isClick(node)
Checks whether node can be clicked.
service.toClick()
Clicks the focused node. On Android 7 and later, a simulated screen tap is preferred.
service.toClick(node)
Clicks the specified node.
service.toLongClick()
Long-clicks the focused node.
service.toLongClick(node)
Long-clicks the specified node.
service.toBack()
Goes back.
service.toHome()
Goes to the Home screen.
service.toNotification()
Opens the notification shade.
service.toParent()
Opens the recent-apps screen.
service.scrollBackward(node)
Scrolls backward.
service.scrollForward(node)
Scrolls forward.
service.loadGesturePackage(name)
Loads the named gesture scheme.
service.click(x,y)
Simulates a tap at the specified screen coordinates. Requires Android 7 or later.
service.longClick(x,y)
Simulates a long press at the specified screen coordinates. Requires Android 7 or later.
service.press(x,y,t)
Presses the specified screen coordinates for t milliseconds. Requires Android 7 or later.
service.swipe(x1,y1,x2,y2,t)
Simulates a swipe from x1,y1 to x2,y2 lasting t milliseconds. Requires Android 7 or later.
Code control statements.
if condition then
 code to run
end
Runs the enclosed code when condition is true. Example:
if service.isEditView(node) then
 service.execute("Split edit",node)
 return true
end
This opens Split edit when the focus is an edit field.
for n=1,count do
 code to run
end
Repeats code count times. Example:
for n=1,10 do
 service.toBack()
end
This goes back ten times.
Defining a function:
function functionName(arguments)
 function code
end
A function is a reusable block of code. This example appends the contents of one list to another ten times:
function append(t1,t2)
 for k,v in ipairs(t2) do
 table.insert(t1,v)
 end
end
clickList={}
buttonList={"%Click","%Back"}
for n=1,10 do
 append(clickList,buttonList)
end
function swipeDown()
 service.swipe(500,300,500,1000,1000)
 return true
end
This simulates a downward swipe and can be used in gesture code. Example:
service.click({{">WeChat","%swipeDown"}})
Open WeChat, then swipe downward.
Automatic clicking:
service.click({buttonList})
Finds and clicks the listed buttons in order. Button names support operators: # before a name searches custom labels; * before or after a name matches extra text; # after a name selects a result by index; @ limits a search to an app; $ adds a delay. Multiple lists and result indexes are supported. Returns true on success and false on failure.
Delayed clicking:
service.postClick(delay,{buttonList})
Runs the click sequence after delay milliseconds. buttonList uses the same syntax as service.click. This method has no return value.
service.plugin("extensionName",node)
Runs an extension and returns the value supplied by that extension.
Automatic clicking is the most flexible way to implement Jieshuo gestures. Its basic form is:
buttonList={}
service.click(buttonList)
return true
These two lines remain fixed; normally you only edit buttonList. A button list contains button names and operators enclosed in braces.
Simplest example:
buttonList={"OK"}
service.click(buttonList)
return true
This code clicks the OK button on the screen.
buttonList={
 "OK",
 "Done"
}
service.click(buttonList)
return true
This is a first-level list. Jieshuo clicks OK if it exists; otherwise it tries Done, then continues through any remaining alternatives.
Sometimes several buttons must be clicked in sequence. This is one advantage of automatic clicking.
buttonList={
 {"Group info","Files"}
}
service.click(buttonList)
return true
This is a second-level list. Its buttons are clicked in order until one cannot be found.
Nesting braces makes sequential click operations possible.
Operators inside buttonList extend its behavior.
The most common operator is * (asterisk). Before or after button text, it means that other text may appear there.
For example, a QQ group entry may include an unread count after its name. Use an asterisk to ignore that suffix:
Jieshuo Screen Reader Group*
# after a name selects a matching result by index. Use it when several buttons have the same name.
For example, OK#1 selects the first OK button. Negative indexes count from the end; OK#-1 selects the last one.
# before text searches a custom label instead of a button name. This is useful for unlabeled controls after you assign them a label.
| means OR. If the text before the bar is present, it is clicked; otherwise the text after the bar is tried. Example:
OK|Done
Click OK or Done.
& means AND. The button before & is clicked only when the current screen also contains the text after it.
OK&*Exit*
Click OK only when the screen contains text matching Exit.
Adding ! after & reverses the condition:
OK&!*Exit*
Click OK only when the screen does not contain Exit.
& at the beginning checks the focused node type. Supported examples include &editable, &clickable, &list, &listItem, and &editField. editField means an edit control that opens the keyboard.
$ after button text specifies how long to wait before the next action.
"Group info$2000","Files"
Click Group info, wait two seconds, then click Files.
< after a button repeats the click the specified number of times. Example:
Next track<10
Click Next track ten times.
< before text locates a button without clicking it. Example:
<OK
Find OK but do not click it.
> after a button specifies how many times to wait for it. Example:
"Group info","Files>10"
After clicking Group info, wait for Files for up to ten seconds; click it as soon as it appears or stop on timeout.
> at the beginning opens an app. Examples:
>WeChat
Open WeChat.
>QQ
Open QQ.
Additional operators can run other actions. % runs a built-in command. For example, %Copy copies text and %Read all reads the entire screen.
% can also call a function defined in the script. The function returns true to continue or false to stop. Example: %customFunction
% can call a script function with arguments. The function returns true to continue or false to stop. Example: %customFunction(arguments).
Text inside [] is activated using a simulated screen tap instead of an accessibility click. This can activate some controls that otherwise cannot be clicked.
[Play] taps Play directly.
[%Click] directly taps the focused node.
[t] uses one number in brackets to press and hold the current focus for t milliseconds.
[6000]
Press and hold the current focus for 6000 milliseconds.
[x,y] taps specified coordinates. Integers are absolute pixels and decimals are relative screen positions.
[300,500] taps 300 pixels from the left and 500 from the top.
[0.3,0.5] taps at 30% of the screen width and 50% of its height.
[x,y,t] presses specified coordinates for t milliseconds.
[300,500,1000] presses the point 300 pixels from the left and 500 from the top for 1000 milliseconds.
[x1,y1,n,a] taps coordinates x1,y1 n times while app a is active. Coordinates may be absolute integers or relative decimals.
[300,500,100,Douyin]
Tap 300,500 one hundred times in Douyin and stop if the app closes. The optional condition supports @appName, &requiredText, and !excludedText.
[x1,y1,x2,y2,t] swipes from x1,y1 to x2,y2 in t milliseconds. Coordinates may be absolute integers or relative decimals.
[300,500,300,800,1000] swipes from 300,500 to 300,800 in 1000 milliseconds.
[x1,y1,x2,y2,t,n] repeats a simulated swipe n times.
[300,500,300,800,1000,10] performs the specified one-second swipe ten times.
[x1,y1,x2,y2,t,n,a] repeats a simulated swipe only while app a is active.
[300,500,300,800,1000,10,Douyin]
Perform the one-second swipe ten times in Douyin and stop if the app closes. The optional condition supports @appName, &requiredText, and !excludedText.
[x1,y1,x2,y2,r,g,b,d] searches the rectangle x1,y1,x2,y2 for RGB color r,g,b within tolerance d, then taps it.
[300,300,800,800,128,128,128,10]
Gesture execution sometimes encounters optional screens. For example, opening a QQ group and then Group info and Files may be interrupted by a group announcement. Branching lists handle these cases. The following handwritten example illustrates the idea and may require adjustment.
buttonList={
 {
 ">QQ",
 "Jieshuo Screen Reader Group*",
 {"I have read the group announcement|Got it"},
 "Group info",
 "Files"
 }
}
Different QQ versions use different buttons to dismiss group announcements. The nested optional list after the group name runs when one of its buttons exists and is skipped otherwise, without stopping later actions. More levels may be nested for complex flows or multiple cases.502
buttonList={
 {
 ">QQ",
 "Jieshuo Screen Reader Group*",
 {
 {"I have read the group announcement","OK"},
 {"Got it","OK"}
 },
 "Group info",
 "Files"
 }
}

string-array.name: gesture_help_items
string-array.item: Gesture operation essentials:\n Single gestures should be straight, and movements should be fast\n The first part of the combined gesture should be longer than half the length of the screen, and the second part can be oriented as long as it is right.

Combination gesture:
 First up, down, last focus
 First down, first, first focus
 First left and right task switching
 Right, then left, back
 First up and then right operation menu
 First right and then right function menu
 First, then left, extension
 First, then left, voice assistant
 First left, then left, word by word
 Right first, then upper, automatically read aloud
 First left and then open the notification bar
 First right, then bottom, browse the list
 Up twice click to browse
 Twice swipe down

Multi-finger gestures require Android 11 or later.
Two-finger double tap: play or pause.
Three-finger swipe down: open notifications.
Three-finger swipe up: go to the Home screen.
Three-finger swipe left: open recent apps.
Three-finger swipe right: go back.

Click on the browse mode gesture:
 Click to switch focus
 Browse up mode
 Browse down mode
Focus browsing mode gestures:\n Up one focus\n Down next focus
QQ WeChat call\n Reject with left swipe\n Answer with right swipe
Phone QQ WeChat call\n Hang up left\n Answer right
List\n Page up to the left\n Flip right to the bottom
Dialog\n Cancel left\n OK right
Progress slider\n Swipe left to decrease slider\n Swipe right to increase slider
Edit box\n Move the cursor forward\n Move the cursor backward

Word-by-word browse mode gestures:
 Click to explain the current character
 Up one line up
 Down one line
 Left previous character
 Right next character
 First left, last, last paragraph
 First right, then next, next paragraph
 First, then right, select text
 Left first, then left, exit literally

Text selection gestures: 
 Single tap: read the current character.
 Up swipe: Go to the previous line.
 Down swipe: Go to the next line.
 Left swipe: Go to the previous character.
 Right swipe: Go to the next character.
 Left up swipe: Go to the previous paragraph.
 Right up swipe: Go to the next paragraph.
 Up right swipe: Deselect all.
 Down right swipe: Copy selection.
 Up left swipe: Append copy.
 Right down swipe: copy the whole text.

Node browsing mode gestures Up swipe: go to the previous node.
 Down swipe: Go to the next node.
 Left swipe: go to the parent node.
 Right swipe: Go to the child node.
 Down left swipe: exit the node.

Voice assistant manual: \n Open AppName: Opens the given app Send Content: allows direct sending to QQ and Wechat Search for content: performs the online search for the given phrase Voice assistant is extensible thanks to the editing menus and plugins.

string-array.name: voice_helper_help_items
string-array.item: Open the given program: Open application name
Install the given program: install Application Name
Uninstall the given program: uninstall Application Name
Read Everything: Read the whole screen
Read aloud: read aloud and follow the cursor
Current Brightness: read the environment\'s brightness.
Click: activate the focused element.
Activate specified item: activate item with the specified name
Copy currently focused item: Copy the currently focused item to the clipboard
Translate: Translate the currently focused text.
Translate LanguageName: Translate the currently focused text to a given language
Select: Selects the given text
Send a message in the qq WeChat chat window: Hello send
ENter Text: Enters the spoken text in the text box
Long Input: Long dictation mode
Check weather: checks the weather
Check the ticket: checks the train tickets.
Tell the recipe: check the recipe for a given food.
Tell a joke: tells a random joke
Copy the response: copies the response of a given command.
There are more features waiting for being discovered.
